Header.Name: Actor
Header.Description: This is a test profile for Person-related data according to the CIDOC (and PiCo) models.

Component.name: Actor
Component.clariah:label: Actor observation
Component.clariah:explanation: This is an entry form for actor's observations. Registering observations is Tastade's approach to source-critical historical research. Actors are people or groups (organisations). According to the PiCo model: "A Person Observation is the representation of how a person is recorded in an original source. [...] Person Observations include data as much as possible as it appears in the source, that is, with the age, occupation, and spelling of the person's name as recorded in the deed." Use this same approach for groups/organisations as well. See documentation at: https://edu.nl/avfnw

Component.name: ObservationLinkToSource
Component.clariah:label: Source of the observation
Component.clariah:explanation: Every observation in Tastade must be linked to a source. See documentation at: https://edu.nl/avfnw

Element.name: to
Element.clariah:label: Link
Element.clariah:explanation: Start typing any word from the key title of the source (for example, a country code such as NL) and select it once it appears. See documentation at: https://edu.nl/avfnw

Component.name: ObservationLocator
Component.clariah:label: Observation locator
Component.clariah:explanation: If applicable, add information about the specific location, within a source, of the observation data that you are registering in this record. Do not add if the link is the same as the source's folder. See documentation at: https://edu.nl/avfnw

Element.name: pageScanUrl
Element.clariah:label: Observation locator link
Element.clariah:explanation: If applicable, add the link(s) to the specific scan(s) where the observation data that you are registering in this record occurs. See documentation at: https://edu.nl/avfnw

Element.name: locator
Element.clariah:label: Observation locator text
Element.clariah:explanation: If applicable, add the page, folio, line number, or any other pointer to the specific part in a source where the observation occurs. If you entered the page Url above, here you could enter the page number as a label/string. See documentation at: https://edu.nl/avfnw

Component.name: ActorType
Component.clariah:label: Type of Actor
Component.clariah:explanation: Select if it is a Person or a Group/Organisation. In some cases it may be difficult to determine (select then Unknown). See documentation at: https://edu.nl/avfnw

Element.name: labelAsWritten
Element.clariah:label: Name as observed
Element.clariah:explanation: Write here the name of the Actor as observed in the source (as written, transcribed, or extracted). If you are entering data about an entity, but there is no written name for it, state "unknown" or "unnamed" following project internal conventions. See documentation at: https://edu.nl/avfnw

Element.name: confidenceValue
Element.clariah:explanation: How confident you (or an algorithm) are of an observation (what you observed (read) in the source), or of a reconstruction. Reflect the uncertainties and ambiguities of the inferred observation (or reconstruction) by choosing one of the values.

Component.name: RoleInSource
Component.clariah:explanation: If applicable, enter the role of an Actor observation on the Source. For persons, you could use a term from the PiCo Roles thesaurus: https://terms.personsincontext.org/roles. See documentation at: https://edu.nl/avfnw

Component.name: Identifiers
Component.clariah:label: Observed identifiers
Component.clariah:explanation: Note here if there are identifiers for the Actor observed in the source. Do not enter VIAF or any other external identifier if it is not written, that is done at the Reconstruction level. See documentation at: https://edu.nl/avfnw

Element.name: identifierType
Element.clariah:label: Type of identifier
Element.clariah:explanation: Note here if it is a local identifier or any other type. See documentation at: https://edu.nl/avfnw

Element.name: identifierValue
Element.clariah:explanation: Add the identifier's label or number. If you chose "Other" in the Identifier type, enter here, in parenthesis, what kind of identifier it is; for example: 457 (Register entry number). See documentation at: https://edu.nl/avfnw

Component.name: PersonNamePart
Component.clariah:explanation: This group of fields is used to enter the specific parts of the name attributed to the documented person.
Enter the values for each type that can be identified in the person name

Element.name: prefix
Element.clariah:explanation: A Prefix is a noble or honorific title prefixing a name, e.g. 'Prof. dr.' or 'Jhr.'

Element.name: initials
Element.clariah:explanation: An initial is the first letter of a person's given name (or sometimes a combination of letters). The Initials property can be used to separately record the initial(s) of a person's given name(s). Each initial should be followed by a dot. It is recommended to always use the Initials property to record initials, but if only the initials of a given name are known, they may also be recorded using pnv:givenName (or pnv:firstName).

Element.name: givenName
Element.clariah:explanation: A Given name designates the name(s) given to someone at birth or any other name-giving event. In the U.S., the first name of a Person.

Element.name: patronym
Element.clariah:explanation: A Patronym is a name element based on the given name of one's father or grandfather. This is also the preferred property for a matronym (i.e. a name element based on the given name of one's mother or grandmother).

Element.name: givenNameSufix
Element.clariah:explanation: A Given name suffix is a name part that is appended to a given name. In the name of the fifteenth-century Duke of Burgundy Philip the Good, for example, 'the Good' is the Given name suffix.

Element.name: infixTitle
Element.clariah:explanation: An Infix title designates a title in the middle of a name.

Element.name: surname
Element.clariah:explanation: A surname is the name of the family a person is born into, including one or more prefixes. In some cases the honorific prefix can be incorporated into the surname (e.g. Van Welderen baron Rengers).

Element.name: surnamePrefix
Element.clariah:explanation: A Surname prefix is a name part prefixing the surname (e.g. 'van' or 'van den').

Element.name: baseSurname
Element.clariah:explanation: A Base surname is a family name without any prefixes, if those prefixes need to be ignored in sorting. If the family name is e.g. 'de Vries' and it needs to be sorted under 'V', the Base surname is 'Vries'.

Element.name: trailingPatronym
Element.clariah:explanation: A Trailing patronym refers to the parent's given name, suffixing the person's family name, mostly used for disambiguation.

Element.name: honorificSuffix
Element.clariah:explanation: An honorific suffix following a Person's name such as M.D./PhD/MSCSW.

Element.name: disambiguatingDescription
Element.clariah:explanation: A Disambiguating description is a name part that is appended to make sure that the right person is designated. Name parts like 'Sr.' and 'Jr.', used to distinguish a child from his parent, are disambiguating descriptions.

Element.name: confidenceValue
Element.clariah:explanation: How confident you (or an algorithm) are of having split the name parts correctly.

Component.name: PersonData
Component.clariah:label: Person data observed
Component.clariah:explanation: This group of fields is for entering person-related data as observed in the source. See documentation at: https://edu.nl/avfnw

Component.name: BirthDate
Component.clariah:label: Date of birth
Component.clariah:explanation: Enter birth date information as seen in the source, and add your interpretation on how it should be normalized. See documentation at: https://edu.nl/avfnw

Element.name: labelAsWritten
Element.clariah:label: Date text
Element.clariah:explanation: Enter the date as it appears in the source, verbatim (e.g., "omtrent 1810", "before Easter 1785", "the third of May in the year of Our Lord 1780"). This preserves the original wording for traceability.

Element.name: confidenceValue
Element.clariah:explanation: How confident you (or an algorithm) are of having correctly typed the date as recorded.

Component.name: DateNormalized
Component.clariah:explanation: Enter your interpretation about how this date should be normalized. See documentation at: https://edu.nl/avfnw

Element.name: datePrecision
Element.clariah:explanation: Select the type of precision that applies to your normalized date. This helps validate that dateStart/dateEnd are filled correctly. See documentation at: https://edu.nl/avfnw

Element.name: dateStart
Element.clariah:explanation: Enter earliest possible date in EDTF format. Rules: 1) For an EXACT date: enter the date in dateStart, leave dateEnd empty. 2) For a RANGE: enter earliest in dateStart, latest in dateEnd. 3) For "BEFORE X": leave dateStart empty, enter X in dateEnd. 4) For "AFTER Y": enter Y in dateStart, leave dateEnd empty. 5) EDTF uncertainty markers (?, ~, %) can be used in either field, follow the instructions here: https://knaw.sharepoint.com/:w:/s/PRJ-Brievenportaal/IQB7jUVOq98BR4Oy786Ch8n1AcilMidno3GLLVdmgUaYF-8?e=FBjVTA

Element.name: dateEnd
Element.clariah:explanation: Enter latest possible date in EDTF format. See rules in documentation of field "dateStart". For EDTF conventions, follow the instructions here: https://knaw.sharepoint.com/:w:/s/PRJ-Brievenportaal/IQB7jUVOq98BR4Oy786Ch8n1AcilMidno3GLLVdmgUaYF-8?e=FBjVTA

Element.name: noteDate
Element.clariah:explanation: Add any clarifying notes related to the dates. These notes may be for internal or external use (t.b.d.)

Element.name: confidenceValue
Element.clariah:explanation: How confident you (or an algorithm) that this date is normalised correctly.

Element.name: hasAgeNormalized
Element.clariah:explanation: The age of a person. Only used for Person observations, in case the birth date is not known, but the age is. In combination with de date of the Source, a birth date range can be derived, which can be used in the process of creating a Person reconstruction. The age is considered to be in years, unless otherwise mentioned. So an age of "4" is considered to be 4 years, where "4 months" is interpreted as 4 months. Numerical ages ("4") are preferred above ages in text ("four").
